_note: Researched rulings that replace CFBD /coaches rows for seasons whose records don't reconcile with games played: double-credited co-coached bowls, rows misfiled under the wrong school or year, non-contiguous tenures, and seasons CFBD has no row for. Each ruled season is { segments, receipts, note? }. Segments run from 'start' (the date of the coach's first game, resolved to a game ordinal at build time so it survives spine gaps; a plain startOrd also works) until the next segment; 'interim: true' forces the flag when the started-mid-season heuristic can't see it. Receipts are the season's Wikipedia page naming the coach ('Head coach X' from the infobox, or the bare name), checked by scripts/data/check-receipts.mjs; a season with receipts: [] is on the coverage report's work list. The note carries the ruling's facts where the sources disagree with CFBD. The 2026-09-28 batch: CFBD dropped one coach from each of these two-coach seasons and left a single row covering part of it; ordinals follow that row's record against the result sequence (Paterno 8-1 = games 1-9 of 2011, Bradley the last four; Sarkisian 3-2 = USC's first five of 2015, Helton from game 6; Hope 6-6 = Purdue's twelve regular-season games of 2012, Higgins the Heart of Dallas Bowl; and so on).

_note_interim_bowls: Interim-coached final games, researched 2026-09-28 against each season's Wikipedia page (infobox head_coach2 and the bowl section) or the bowl game's own page. CFBD credits the departing coach with the whole season; the bowl goes to the coach who stood on the sideline. Where that coach was already the permanent successor (Gutekunst 1985, Hackett 1989, Tepper 1991, Torbush 1997, Scelfo 1998, B. Williams 1999, Stewart 2007, Levine 2011) no interim flag is set, since his stint runs on into the next season. Louisiana-Monroe 2015 is not a bowl: Berry was fired after the 10th game (Arkansas State) and John Mumford coached the final three.
